court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Family Court at Erode, H.M.O.P.No.604 of 2014
facts_of_case: Appellant/husband sought divorce on ground of cruelty; respondent/wife developed suspicion about his conduct and character, humiliated him by connecting him with female colleagues.

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty can be physical or mental.
legal_principles.held: The expression 'cruelty' has not been defined in the Act. Cruelty can be physical or mental.
cited_cases: A.Jayachandra versus Annel kaur, (2005) 2 Supreme Court Cases 22

legal_principles.principle: Cruelty includes mental cruelty, which falls within the purview of a matrimonial wrong.
legal_principles.held: Cruelty, as noted above, includes mental cruelty, which falls within the purview of a matrimonial wrong.
cited_cases: A.Jayachandra versus Annel kaur, (2005) 2 Supreme Court Cases 22

legal_principles.principle: Courts are required to probe into the mental process and mental effect of incidents that are brought out in evidence.
legal_principles.held: It is in this view that one has to consider the evidence in matrimonial disputes.
cited_cases: A.Jayachandra versus Annel kaur, (2005) 2 Supreme Court Cases 22

legal_principles.principle: The concept of proof beyond the shadow of doubt is to be applied to criminal trials and not to civil matters, including divorce cases.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, one has to see what are the probabilities in a case and legal cruelty has to be found out, not merely as a matter of fact, but as the effect on the mind of the complaining spouse because of the acts or omissions of the other.
cited_cases: A.Jayachandra versus Annel kaur, (2005) 2 Supreme Court Cases 22
keywords: proof beyond the shadow of doubt

outcome.final_order: Decree and judgment dated 15.06.2016 set aside.
